entries.body: Finiko, a Russian operation that turned out to be a Ponzi scheme, collapsed in July 2021 after defrauding approximately $95 million from people. Investors, facing difficult economic conditions in Russia, were promised they could see returns of up to 30% a month.

entries.title: Hacker nets $6.3 million in Belt Finance exploit
entries.body: Belt Finance fell victim to a <button class="define-target" id="flash-loan">flash loan</button> attack which netted an attacker $6.3 million. This was yet another exploit targeting a protocol built on the Binance Smart Chain protocol, following other attacks over the previous five months on C.R.E.A.M. Finance, bEarn, Bogged Finance, Uranium Finance, Meerkat Finance, SafeMoon, Spartan Protocol, BurgerSwap, and PancakeBunny.

links.linkText: "Belt Finance loses millions in latest BSC-based DeFi exploit"

BurgerSwap said it would "strive to cover all [users'] loss".

entries.body: Attackers exploited a flaw in the <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">smart contract</button> of Bogged Finance's BOG token to drain half the <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">liquidity pool</button>, equivalent about $3 million. This resulted in the BOG token tanking in value from about $1.80 to $0.0003.
entries.title: Attackers drain $3 million from BOG liquidity pool

image.alt: Logo for Pancake Bunny: two exclamation points overlaid on a sideways parenthesis, forming a bunny face
image.caption: PancakeBunny logo

entries.body: A hacker used <button class="define-target" id="flash-loan">flash loans</button> to manipulate the price of other token pools, to then exploit a bug in PancakeBunny logic that calculates how many tokens should be minted. They were able to mint and then sell 7 million tokens, making off with $45 million and tanking the price of BUNNY tokens from $146 to $0.90. PancakeBunny tweeted shortly after the attack that they would be "working on a reimbursement plan" for those affected.
entries.title: $45 million stolen from PancakeBunny Finance

entries.title: Hacker drains $10.85 million from bEarn Fi
entries.body: An attacker pulled $10.85 million in funds out of one of bEarn Fi's vaults by exploiting a bug that allowed them to withdraw more funds than they deposited. bEarn promised to compensate affected users with 105% of the amount they lost.

links.linkText: "DeFi platform ‘bEarn Fi’ promises 105% compensation after $10 million hack, but is it the right thing?"

entries.title: $24.5 million emptied from xToken platform
entries.body: A <button class="define-target" id="flash-loan">flash loan</button> attack allowed hackers to exploit two vulnerabilities in the xToken <button class="define-target" id="defi">DeFi</button> platform and steal $24.5 million. This was the first of two large-scale hacks of the platform this year.
